statement.population: positive rational edge triples modulo positive rational scaling, with edge permutation retained as a separate symmetry
statement.normalization: for e=(a,b,c) in Q_{>0}^3, choose L=lcm(den(a),den(b),den(c)), put X=La,Y=Lb,Z=Lc, g=gcd(X,Y,Z), and Prim(e)=(A,B,C)=(X/g,Y/g,Z/g)
claims: Prim(lambda*e)=Prim(e) for every lambda in Q_{>0}
the primitive positive integer representative of a positive rational ray is unique
Prim is equivariant for permutations of the three edge coordinates
if all three pairwise edge-square sums and the total edge-square sum are rational squares, then after primitive normalization their four square roots are integers

proof.common_denominator_independence: If D is any other positive common denominator, then (Da,Db,Dc)=k(X,Y,Z) for some positive integer k after replacing D by a common multiple if necessary; dividing by the coordinate gcd removes k, so the primitive triple is independent of the chosen common denominator.
proof.scaling_invariance: Write lambda=m/n with gcd(m,n)=1. Starting from integer lift (X,Y,Z), the common denominator nL gives integer lift m(X,Y,Z) for lambda*e. Its coordinate gcd is m*g, hence Prim(lambda*e)=(X/g,Y/g,Z/g)=Prim(e).
proof.uniqueness: If primitive positive integer triples u=(A,B,C) and v=(A',B',C') lie on the same positive rational ray, v=(p/q)u with gcd(p,q)=1. Integrality of v gives q divides pA,pB,pC; gcd(p,q)=1 implies q divides gcd(A,B,C)=1, so q=1. Applying the same argument to u=(1/p)v gives p=1. Thus u=v.
proof.permutation_equivariance: LCM of denominators and coordinate gcd are symmetric in the coordinates, so Prim(sigma(e))=sigma(Prim(e)) for every sigma in S3.
proof.rational_square_integrality: If N is a nonnegative integer and r in Q satisfies r^2=N, write r=u/v in lowest terms. Then u^2=N*v^2, hence v^2 divides u^2; gcd(u,v)=1 forces v=1. Therefore every rational square root of an integer is an integer.
proof.cuboid_transfer: For primitive (A,B,C)=Prim(e), positive rational scaling multiplies every face/space diagonal by the same rational factor used on the edges. Thus A^2+B^2, A^2+C^2, B^2+C^2, and A^2+B^2+C^2 are integers that remain rational squares; by rational_square_integrality their square roots D_AB,D_AC,D_BC,D_ABC are integers.
